open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal global project scope
open_points.text: State 0 says “a global producer exists only through an explicitly granted capability”; M13 says “With `all_projects` the scope mode alone admits an import for any project the Registry reports active; no grant is consulted and no further capability is needed.”
open_points.question: Does `all_projects` itself confer global publication scope, or must the principal also receive a distinct explicitly granted global capability?
options: `all_projects` alone authorizes imports to every active Registry project
`all_projects` additionally requires an explicitly granted global capability
open_points.default_guess: Treat the administrator-selected `all_projects` mode as the explicit global grant and require no additional capability.

witness.initial: An active Registry project P exists; an administrator creates an active `all_projects` estimate producer and issues a credential, but creates no ProducerProjectGrant and grants no separate global capability.
events: The producer submits a valid snapshot import for P.
outcomes: M13 admits the import because `all_projects` and P's active Registry status are sufficient.
State 0 rejects the import because no explicit global capability was granted.
witness.observer: The producer and the administrator reviewing the import result and audit.

open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal disable/enable provenance
open_points.text: The lifecycle is `active ↔ disabled`, but the only transition provenance fields are `disabled_at | None` and `disabled_by | None`; the text does not say what happens to them when the principal is enabled again.
open_points.question: After `disabled → active`, are `disabled_at` and `disabled_by` cleared, retained as the most recent disablement, or represented through additional enablement facts?
options: Retain the most recent disablement values while status is active
Add separate enablement provenance while retaining disablement history
open_points.default_guess: Clear `disabled_at` and `disabled_by` on re-enablement and rely on AuditRecord for history.

witness.initial: Service principal S is active with both disablement fields null.
events: Administrator A disables S at t1.
Administrator B enables S at t2.
outcomes: The active view has `disabled_at = null` because enabling cleared current-state disablement provenance.
The active view still has `disabled_at = t1` because the fields retain the last disablement.
witness.observer: The administrator reading the service-principal view.

open_points.subject: ProducerProjectGrant creation for all-projects principals
open_points.text: M13 says grants are consulted only for `granted_projects` and that `all_projects` consults no grant, but it never says whether the producer-grant action rejects or creates an inert grant for an `all_projects` principal.
open_points.question: May an administrator create a ProducerProjectGrant for a ServicePrincipal whose immutable `scope_mode` is `all_projects`?
options: Reject the grant because it can never affect authorization
Create and retain the grant even though authorization ignores it
open_points.default_guess: Reject producer-grant creation unless the principal has `scope_mode = granted_projects`.

witness.initial: An active `all_projects` ServicePrincipal S and active Registry project P exist, with no grant for the pair.
events: An administrator invokes the producer-project grant action for S and P.
outcomes: The action is rejected because grants are inapplicable to S's immutable scope mode.
A ProducerProjectGrant is created and audited but remains authorization-inert.
witness.observer: The administrator and anyone later listing or auditing producer grants.

open_points.subject: Pre-activation resolution of allocations to newly created snapshot sections
open_points.text: “Activation of an imported version creates plans” and unmatched source sections create new `PortalSection` records, but allocations to absent old sections “must be explicitly re-allocated by an operator before that version can be activated”; the text also says “no other mapping operation exists.”
open_points.question: How can an operator reallocate to an unmatched section before activation if that section and its plan are created only by activation?
options: Candidate-version creation materializes the new sections and plans before activation
Activation accepts and applies the required reallocations atomically
Activation first persists linking records even when activation is refused
Such a candidate cannot be activated when any allocation needs an unmatched new section
open_points.default_guess: Materialize candidate sections and plans when the imported BudgetVersion is created, while keeping the version inactive until allocations are resolved.

witness.initial: Project P has an active manual budget with section A and an expense allocated to A; an imported candidate contains only unmatched source section B.
events: A staff member reviews the imported candidate.
The staff member attempts to resolve the expense before activation.
The staff member attempts to activate the candidate.
outcomes: If B is materialized with the inactive candidate, the staff member reallocates the expense to B and activation succeeds.
If B is created only by activation, the staff member cannot target B beforehand, while activation is refused because the allocation to A remains unresolved.
witness.observer: The staff member performing budget activation.

open_points.subject: First-administrator bootstrap audit
open_points.text: R0-07 says the bootstrap command is “never printed, logged or audited”; M36 says “The first-administrator bootstrap of R0-07 is no exception: it writes one `staff.create` record.”
open_points.question: Does successful creation of the first administrator append an AuditRecord?
options: Create no AuditRecord, as required by R0-07
Create one system-actor `staff.create` AuditRecord, as required by M36
open_points.default_guess: Follow the explicit State 0 decision and create no AuditRecord for bootstrap.

witness.initial: The deployment contains no staff accounts or audit records.
events: The host operator runs the local bootstrap command with valid inputs.
The command successfully creates the first active administrator.
An auditor inspects persisted audit records.
outcomes: Under R0-07, no audit record exists for the bootstrap.
Under M36, one system-actor `staff.create` record names the new `staff_id`.
witness.observer: The auditor or host operator inspecting the database.
